thread.section_title: Stock Market Today - Investor's Business Daily
thread.title: Stocks Up; Will Tesla Someday Hit 4,000?

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Stocks Up; Will Tesla Someday Hit 4,000?
text:
Blue chips and the S&P 500 led the march up midday Wednesday, but the FANG stocks and Apple ( AAPL ) were mostly down.
X The   average popped 1.2%, while the S&P 500 rose 0.9%. The Nasdaq trailed, advancing 0.5%. Volume in the stock market today was running behind the previous session's pace.
The stock of Tesla Motors ( TSLA ) drove ahead 3% in above-average volume. The electric-car maker's stock is about 11% off its high as it works on a new consolidation. Catherine Wood, CEO at Ark Investment Management, told CNBC this morning that Tesla could some day trade at 4,000 per share . Tesla is currently trading above 340.
Tesla will report quarterly results after today's close. The Street expects a quarterly loss of $3.12 a share and a full-year 2017 loss of $8.66 a share. Tesla reported annual losses in 2015-16 and is expected to stay in the red in 2017-18.
In the 30-component   average, Boeing ( BA ) rang up the biggest gain, up 3.3% in heavy volume. Boeing's relative strength line is at a new high. The RS line measures a stock's performance vs. the S&P 500.
FANG Stocks Mixed Among the FANG stocks, Facebook ( FB ) dropped 1.3% in fast turnover as it climbed from its 50-day moving average, Amazon.com ( AMZN ) inched up 0.3% in heavy volume, Netflix ( NFLX ) added 0.9% in brisk volume, and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) fell 1% in hefty volume. Apple slid 1% in quick trade.
Within IBD's 197 industry groups, chipmakers, dairy companies and restaurants were the weak players. The day's strong industries included toys, cars and apparel.
Radware Breaks Out Breakouts were scarce midday Wednesday. Thinly traded Radware Ltd. ( RDWR ) climbed above a 20.88 buy point in heavy volume. The Israel-based network security provider reported adjusted earnings of 9 cents a share, a 50% increase vs. the year-ago period and above the consensus estimate for 7 cents a share.
A Rising Group One group that has been moving up in the rankings showed additional strength midday Wednesday. Six weeks ago, the superregional banks were No. 50 among 197 industry groups. Going into Wednesday, the superregional banks were No. 17.
Banks rising Wednesday included SunTrust Banks ( STI ), up 2.5%; Fifth Third Bancorp ( FITB ), up 1.8%; U.S. Bancorp ( USB ), up 1.6%; and Comerica ( CMA ), up 1.7%.
